questions.question: May crumbkit/board#294 (shared repo-listing and day helpers moved into python/board-plugin) and then #297 (tasks/task/v2 Markdown tasks and the tasks.available call, which syncs in-scope repos with a 5 s deadline and keeps each context's tasks in its silo) be merged? Before #297 merges, please check one thing in Reflect on your phone: it shows a tasks/ folder, and it keeps a task file's frontmatter when you edit the task.
questions.why: Two clean-context Opus reviews ran, and the second found nothing that must be fixed. All 7 CI checks pass on #294 (88337546) and #297 (49f7297b). #294 adds 37 net lines and #297 adds 593. Measured with one GitHub remote, a warm call takes 0.76 s at the median and 0.84 to 0.97 s at p95, within the 1.0 s budget. A cold call took 1.13 s at p95, and several remotes were not measured (/evals/tasks-available-latency). A hung remote makes later calls take about 5 s, and the README says so. Bounding Board's git fetch is a separate follow-up PR. Board's AGENTS.md leaves merges to the owner.

questions.question: May crumbkit/board#302 (tasks v2 write calls: tasks.add, done, defer, drop and reviewed edit task frontmatter in place, sync before writing and push after, and keep each context's tasks in its silo) be merged? Two choices I made for you: done never moves a repeating task earlier than its defer, and add refuses when two notes repos cover the remote. After it merges, please check that Reflect handles a task file these calls wrote (values are quoted, such as status: "done").
questions.why: Three clean-context Opus reviews ran, and the last approved. Fixed along the way: weekdays skipping Monday, writes to a mount that is not a notes repo, a crash on a task that fails its schema, a retry applying done twice, done moving a task earlier, and a work task silently routed to personal when the origin was unreadable. All 7 CI checks pass on 7b40c6fc. Net +483 production lines against a planned 250, mostly retry handling shared with notes and the input descriptions. Board's AGENTS.md leaves merges to the owner.
